response: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) does not typically predict a decrease in aerobic fitness, as measured by cycle ergometry, in the general population. However, patients with a severe apnea-hypopnea index (greater than 20) have been found to have a statistically significant decrease in aerobic fitness compared to those without OSA. This suggests that while OSA may not have a significant impact on aerobic fitness for most individuals, those with more severe cases of the condition may experience a decline in their aerobic fitness levels. Further research is needed to fully understand the correlation between OSA severity, treatment, and aerobic fitness.
